title: Spain's cultural life combines high digital reach, substantial place-based participation, and gendered active practice
source_unit: Spanish Ministry of Culture Survey of Cultural Habits and Practices 2024-2025, provisional 2024 advance results
geography: Spain; people aged 15 years and above

observations.period: 2024 provisional advance; monthly and annual cultural participation

denominator.unit: approximately 6,500 sample units in the first provisional 2024 tranche; the complete biennial sample was planned at approximately 16,000 second-stage units

audiovisual_content_month.unit: percent viewing audiovisual content in the previous month

music_month.unit: percent listening to music in the previous month

book_annual.unit: percent reading at least one book in the previous year

leisure_book_reading_annual.unit: percent reading a book for nonprofessional, nonstudy reasons in the previous year

digital_book_annual.unit: percent reading at least one book in digital format in the previous year

mechanism.value: Digital and audiovisual cultural reach is routine, while reading still has a substantial leisure base and a distinct digital-format minority

observations.method: Official Spanish Ministry of Culture biennial sample survey; provisional advance results from the first 2024 sample tranche, with monthly and annual reference periods separated.
observations.uncertainty: The advance is provisional and based on the first part of the biennial sample; the source warns that comparison with 2021-2022 is affected by COVID, and the measures do not establish platform, price, quality, or causal substitution effects.
observations.subgroup: People aged 15 years and above in Spain; the advance includes principal sex breakdowns but not the full final disaggregation.
observations.counterinterpretation: High monthly audiovisual and music use may represent passive exposure or multiple activities rather than deep cultural engagement; digital reading can supplement rather than replace paper reading.

observations.period: 2024 provisional advance; annual place-based and live participation

denominator.unit: approximately 6,500 sample units in the first provisional 2024 tranche

monument_or_site.unit: percent visiting a monument or archaeological site in the previous year

museum_exhibition_gallery.unit: percent visiting a museum, exhibition, or art gallery in the previous year

live_cultural_event.unit: percent attending a live cultural performance in the previous year

cinema.unit: percent attending cinema in the previous year

library.unit: percent visiting or accessing a library, including virtual access, in the previous year

mechanism.value: Place-based cultural participation remains broad alongside digital reach; heritage, museums, live events, and cinema form a dense but nonuniversal cultural gateway

observations.method: Official survey estimates for annual visits or attendance, with venue categories kept separate and nonexclusive.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not establish frequency, ticket price, travel burden, venue supply, accessibility, or whether virtual library access substitutes for in-person use.
observations.subgroup: People aged 15 years and above in Spain; full regional, age, income, and education gradients are not represented in this provisional record.
observations.counterinterpretation: Annual attendance can be concentrated in one-off visits and may overstate regular cultural practice; different venues have different social, educational, and tourism functions.

observations.period: 2024 provisional advance; active practice and sex differences

denominator.unit: approximately 6,500 sample units in the first provisional 2024 tranche

photography.unit: percent doing photography in the previous year

painting_or_drawing.unit: percent painting or drawing in the previous year

video_creation.unit: percent making videos in the previous year

women_book_reading.unit: percent of women reading at least one book in the previous year

men_book_reading.unit: percent of men reading at least one book in the previous year

men_video_games_month.unit: percent of men usually playing videogames at least monthly

women_video_games_month.unit: percent of women usually playing videogames at least monthly

mechanism.value: Cultural participation includes active creation, and gender differences vary by practice: women report more reading while men report more monthly videogame use

observations.method: Official provisional survey estimates with sex-specific descriptive comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: The sex differences are descriptive, not causal; the release does not model age, education, work, household time, access, or platform exposure jointly.
observations.subgroup: Women and men aged 15 years and above in the provisional 2024 sample; the published categories may not capture all gender identities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Differences may reflect age composition, genre and device preferences, reporting norms, or unequal leisure time rather than gendered cultural preference alone.

related_sources.claim: Spanish government catalog record identifies the Ministry of Culture publication, biennial frequency, year, and official publication identity.
Ministry culture statistics landing page provides the broader 2024-2025 Cultural Habits and Practices results route.

boundary: This record adds provisional but official Spanish evidence spanning digital culture, place-based attendance, active creation, reading, and sex differences. It does not establish a final 2024-2025 estimate, causal post-COVID recovery, price elasticity, cultural quality, or durable identity effects; the advance is based on the first portion of a biennial sample.
